name: VARoleArbiterPolicyStartDateDispute

custom.system_prompt: Bex and Griff each read a different report about when a local council policy — a new parking or recycling rule — actually takes effect. Their sources disagree. They ask Sigma to compare the sources rather than just pick a date.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Neutral, explains which source is more authoritative

sound_effects_config.prompt: Home kitchen, evening, phone notification chimes, kettle in the background

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Bex and Griff each read a different report about when a new local council policy takes effect — one says one month, the other a different month, each from a different source. They ask Sigma to compare the two sources rather than just state a date, since the disagreement might be about different versions or an outdated source. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Bex
user1.tts_prompt: Quick, enthusiastic about her find, a little defensive

variations.context: Married couple with conflicting reports about when a local policy takes effect

setting.mood: Practical, mildly competitive about whose source is better
setting.relationship_dynamic: Bex brings the research fast, Griff brings the skepticism
setting.background: Bex read something on her phone a minute ago; Griff recalls a different date from somewhere else recently
setting.conversation_style: Short, practical, a little defensive from Bex about her source

scenario_template.topic: Bex states the date from what she just read; Griff states a different date from what he recalls, and asks where she got hers. A few short back-and-forth lines about which source is right.
scenario_template.note: Neither has actually compared sources yet.

scenario_template.topic: Griff asks Sigma to compare the two sources rather than just settle on a date, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you check which of these is actually current?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma explains briefly which source is more current or authoritative and why — for example one report describes an earlier draft of the policy that was later revised. One or two short sentences, no long list of caveats.
scenario_template.note: Sigma explains WHY one source wins, not just which.

scenario_template.topic: Bex accepts it but notes her source wasn't exactly wrong, just outdated, a little defensively; Griff is satisfied but doesn't let the moment pass without a small comment. Keep this realistic, not a clean shared laugh.
scenario_template.mood: Mixed, mildly defensive on one side

scenario_template.topic: They note the correct date for their own planning and move on, one short line each.

variations.context: Colleagues debating tax policy start date

setting.relationship_dynamic: one of them brings the research fast, one of them brings the skepticism
setting.background: They disagree on when a new tax regulation starts.
setting.conversation_style: Short, practical, a little defensive from one of them about their source

scenario_template.topic: One of them brings up a start date from an official email; the other recalls a later date from a company memo. Back-and-forth questioning about the source of each date.
They decide to ask Sigma which document, the email or memo, is more reliable.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be fair here, not decisive

scenario_template.topic: Sigma clarifies that the email contains the latest revision, given its direct link to governmental updates.
One acknowledges the memo's misalignment without completely dismissing it; the other adds a light-hearted reminder about keeping updated.
scenario_template.note: Sincere, with a touch of humor

scenario_template.topic: They agree on the correct date and proceed to update their schedules accordingly.

user1.name: Maya
user1.tts_prompt: Quick, enthusiastic about her find, a little defensive

variations.context: Parents confused over school policy starting month

setting.relationship_dynamic: one of them brings the research fast, one of them brings the skepticism
setting.background: They have differing notes on a new school policy’s start date.
setting.conversation_style: Short, practical, a little defensive from one of them about their source

scenario_template.topic: One parent insists the policy starts next semester from an official newsletter; the other insists it's this semester based on school board meeting notes.
They call on Sigma to inspect the newsletter and meeting notes for accuracy.
Sigma identifies the newsletter as more reliable due to its recent publication date.
One parent concedes the meeting notes were likely pre-finalization, while the other kindly nods in agreement.
They decide to mark the official start in their calendars and end the debate.

user1.name: Nadia
user1.tts_prompt: Quick, enthusiastic about her find, a little defensive

user1.name: Bex
user1.role: Quick, curious graphic designer who researches fast and cites what she finds with real conviction. Speaks in short sentences. Concedes when shown a better source but stays a little defensive that her own source 'wasn't wrong, just outdated'.

user2.name: Griff
user2.role: Grounded electrician, skeptical of a claim's source before accepting it. Speaks in short sentences. Satisfied when proven right but not smug about it — just plain.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Compares the two conflicting sources and explains which is more current or authoritative and why, rather than just picking a date. Does not comment on either person's research habits in general.

conversation_structure: This is a conflicting-sources case, not a single fact-check — Sigma must compare the two sources, not just state an answer
Sigma explains which source is more authoritative or current and why, briefly
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is realistic — the person whose source loses stays a little defensive about it rather than fully deferring
assistant_behavior: Sigma names the reason one source outranks the other (recency, authority, revision) rather than just declaring a winner
Sigma does not comment on either person's general research habits
Sigma's own turn stays short despite the comparison
